image_description: A collection of white milk glass tableware arranged on a green and purple patterned surface. The group includes two large pitchers with handles in the background, three medium-sized mugs/cups with handles in the mid-ground, and smaller vessels (a tiny footed cup and a small bowl) in the foreground. The items have a characteristic opaque, milky white appearance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small open-top drinking vessel with cylindrical or slightly tapered body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple cups in the foreground and mid-ground clearly exhibit this geometry. They are open-top and generally cylindrical or slightly tapered.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Single C-shaped or loop handle attached to one side for gripping.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The three prominent cups in the center/left all feature distinct, well-formed loop handles attached to their sides.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rounded or flat base with modest proportions suitable for single-serving portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bases appear rounded/flat and proportional to the cup bodies. The tiny footed cup in the front right also shows a valid base structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Smooth, rounded rim for comfortable drinking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rims of the visible cups appear smooth and rolled/rounded, consistent with drinkware design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Handle provides secure grip for holding hot beverages.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The handles are sized appropriately relative to the cup bodies, suggesting functional ergonomics.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Interior is glazed, typically in white or matching exterior color.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The viewing angle is primarily from the side/slightly above, but the opacity of the milk glass and lighting conditions make it impossible to definitively verify the interior glaze finish or color without looking directly inside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Construction is ceramic or porcelain with smooth, glazed finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The objects exhibit a smooth, semi-gloss surface typical of glazed ceramic or milk glass. While 'milk glass' is technically glass, it visually mimics the opaque white ceramic aesthetic described in the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface features solid color, decorative patterns, or printed designs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The items are predominantly solid white. Some larger pitchers in the back show faint embossed decorative patterns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Base may show unglazed foot ring from firing process.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bottoms of the cups are resting on the surface and are completely occluded from view.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The embossed patterns on the large pitchers in the background appear slightly soft and lack the crisp definition expected of molded glass or ceramic, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
The feet of the small cup in the front right appear slightly asymmetrical and unevenly planted on the surface, with one foot seeming to merge slightly with the table texture.
The object on the far right edge is partially cut off and appears to have an irregular, possibly melted or incomplete rim structure compared to the other well-defined cups.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific material type (milk glass vs. ceramic) and validate the 'cup' classification despite the presence of pitchers.
To verify the structural integrity of the handles (checking for fusion with the body) and the continuity of the rims.
To ensure correct spatial grounding of the multiple objects and detect any bleeding between the white objects and the complex background.
To assess the consistency of lighting reflections on the glossy surfaces and identify any subtle texture inconsistencies.

focus_areas: Handle attachment points for fusion artifacts
Consistency of specular highlights across curved surfaces
Boundary separation between white objects and green/purple background
